clue.text: Amphibian taking oxygen in small amount

indicators.note: the small amount is said to take in, or hold, the oxygen symbol

parts.note: a tad is a small amount
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A frog-like creature breathing in a little oxygen.
explanation.definitionFit: A toad is a warty, land-loving amphibian, a close cousin of the frog.

clue.text: Moderate's consumed with rage

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: temper means a fit of rage
ate means consumed

explanation.surface: A moderate politician is eaten up with fury.
explanation.definitionFit: Temperate as an adjective means restrained or mild, avoiding extremes.

clue.text: Woman picks engagement rings up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters are read from bottom to top
rings means the clue words encircle the name within them

explanation.surface: A woman chooses engagement rings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rings' finds SENGA within 'picks engagement'; 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Agnes is a woman's first name, so any woman so called fits.

clue.text: Hard ground making farmer endlessly irate

indicators.note: making is read as forming something new, so the letters that follow are rearranged
endlessly says the word irate loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before its last letter goes

explanation.surface: Solid soil is what makes an agricultural worker furious without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims IRATE to IRAT; 'making' then rearranges FARMER plus IRAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase for dry land, used of solid ground beneath one's feet after a voyage or flight.

clue.text: Greek character embraced by female creature

indicators.note: embraced by means the Greek letter sits inside the woman's name

parts.note: Edna is a female name
chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek man is hugged by a woman's being.
explanation.definitionFit: The echidna, or spiny anteater, is an egg-laying mammal of Australia and New Guinea.

clue.text: East German comes in ready to make swift reply

indicators.note: comes in means the East German word enters the word for ready

parts.note: fruit that is ripe is ready
Ost is German for east

explanation.surface: An East German arrives, poised to answer smartly.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a quick, sharp retort, originally a fencer's quick return thrust.

clue.text: Peers interfere outrageously in capitalist system

indicators.note: outrageously suggests wild disorder, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Lords meddle scandalously in the economy.
explanation.definitionFit: An economy in which private business operates with little state regulation is the essence of capitalism.

clue.text: Tory Stanley Matthews would run down?

definitions.meaning: a Conservative, someone on the political right
Stanley Matthews, the English footballer, played outside right, running down that flank of the pitch

explanation.surface: A Conservative recalls the great footballer's dashes along the touchline.
explanation.walkthrough: Stanley Matthews was an English footballer of the 1930s to 1960s, famed for dribbling down the right flank.
explanation.definitionFit: Conservatives belong to the political right, and the wing on the right is where Matthews played.

clue.text: Local dignitary hiding man in tree

indicators.note: hiding means the word man is concealed, taken out of sight

parts.note: an alderman is a senior member of a local council

explanation.surface: A civic official conceals a fellow in the branches.
explanation.definitionFit: The alder is a waterside tree of the birch family.

clue.text: Librarian, ample, trained to become dancer

indicators.note: trained means shaped or worked into new form, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A well-built book-lender, coached, turns into a ballet performer.
explanation.definitionFit: The leading female dancer of a ballet company holds this title.

clue.text: Royal against appearing in military display

indicators.note: the word for against appears inside the word for the display

parts.note: a march is a military parade or display
on can mean against, as in leaning on a wall

explanation.surface: A member of the royal family is opposed to showing up at a military parade.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as a noun, a royal is a king or queen, the reigning sovereign.

clue.text: Nick in place departs as promised

indicators.note: in places the word for nick inside the place-and-departs letters

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs
to nick a ball in cricket is to edge it

explanation.surface: Someone nicked in a spot leaves, as they said they would.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, to edge or nick the ball is to touch it faintly with the bat.
explanation.definitionFit: To have pledged something is to have vowed or committed to it.

clue.text: Feel glum about securing second place for racing

indicators.note: securing means the turned word holds the letter for second
about means the word for feeling glum is turned round

parts.note: to mope is to feel glum

explanation.surface: Feeling down about getting runner-up at the races.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns MOPE to EPOM; 'securing' puts S inside it. Epsom is an English racecourse in Surrey, home of the Derby.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom Downs is the Surrey racecourse that stages the Derby and the Oaks.

clue.text: Rebel is mailed drug that doctor seizes

indicators.note: seizes means the doctor's letters grab and hold the rest

parts.note: something mailed has been sent
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: An insurgent receives a drug by post, and a doctor confiscates it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissenter refuses to conform, rebelling against established views or a church.

clue.text: Describe in general an unintelligent judge

parts.note: A is the indefinite article, like an
dumb is slang for unintelligent
to rate is to judge or assess

explanation.surface: Portraying a dim-witted magistrate in broad strokes.
explanation.definitionFit: To adumbrate is to outline or sketch something only roughly, without detail.

clue.text: Top meal — no starter — succeeded in test

indicators.note: no starter means the meal word loses its first letter

parts.note: supper is an evening meal

indicators.note: in places the succeeded letter inside the test

parts.note: the MOT is the annual British roadworthiness test for vehicles
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A first-class dinner without a first course passes the exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no starter' doubles as a dinner menu joke; MOT is the UK's yearly car safety test.
explanation.definitionFit: Uppermost means highest, at the top of something.

clue.text: One wrongly taking tea in London

definitions.meaning: someone who takes what is not theirs, a robber
in Cockney rhyming slang a tea leaf means a robber, so tea is its clipped form

explanation.surface: A Londoner mistakenly helping himself to a cuppa.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang is London East End speech: 'tea leaf' rhymes with the answer, and in use is often shortened to its first word.
explanation.definitionFit: A thief steals, taking property unlawfully, and in London slang is a tea leaf.

clue.text: Maybe Peter's poem recalled Yankee commander

definitions.note: the apostle Peter is an example; the 's stands for is

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the poem title is reversed

parts.note: If is Kipling's famous poem
William Sherman was a Union general in the American Civil War

explanation.surface: Peter's poem remembered an American officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yankee' means a Union (northern) soldier in the American Civil War; 'recalled' turns IF to FI.
explanation.definitionFit: Simon Peter caught fish on Galilee before Jesus made him a fisher of men.

clue.text: Boot out former Brazilian player unable to finish

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: unable to finish means the player's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Pele was the great Brazilian footballer

explanation.surface: Sacking an ex-Brazil footballer who couldn't complete the match.
explanation.definitionFit: To boot out someone is to throw them out, eject or banish them.

clue.text: Something eaten when secretary's requited love

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
PA, personal assistant, is a secretary; the 's stands for is, a link

indicators.note: requited means paid back or returned, so the word for love is reversed

parts.note: sugar is a term of endearment, like love

explanation.surface: Something to eat on the day an office assistant's affection is returned.
explanation.definitionFit: Asparagus is a vegetable whose young spears are eaten, so it is food.

clue.text: Cunning Italian author entertains duke in style

indicators.note: entertains means the outer pieces host the duke inside them

parts.note: art can mean cunning or craft
Umberto Eco was an Italian novelist

explanation.surface: A crafty Italian writer hosts an aristocrat in fine fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Art Deco is the geometric design movement of the 1920s and 1930s.

clue.text: Ruthless type from country seen in pub area

indicators.note: seen in means the country appears inside the pub letters

parts.note: PH is the map abbreviation for public house
Iran is a country

explanation.surface: A merciless man from abroad spotted in the bar zone.
explanation.definitionFit: A piranha is figuratively a predatory, ruthless person, after the voracious fish.

clue.text: Fish to get in for one doing the Lord's work

parts.note: the carp is a freshwater fish
to enter is to get in

explanation.surface: Catching fish to gain entry as a servant of God.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Lord' is Jesus, who worked as a carpenter in Nazareth before his ministry.
explanation.definitionFit: Jesus was a woodworker by trade, so this trade was literally the Lord's work.

clue.text: Primate uniting church with devil

parts.note: an imp is a little devil

explanation.surface: An archbishop brings together the church and Satan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' looks like an archbishop in the church setting; it is the ape.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimpanzee is an ape, one of the primate order.

clue.text: Singer's asset managed by vacuous Geordie

parts.note: to have run a business is to have managed it

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so only the outer letters of Geordie remain

explanation.surface: A vocalist's strength handled by an empty-headed Newcastle man.
explanation.walkthrough: A Geordie is someone from Newcastle upon Tyne in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A singer's range is the span of notes their voice can reach, a valuable quality.

clue.text: Bouquet welcomes king from old Scandinavia

indicators.note: welcomes means the bouquet word takes the king letter inside

parts.note: a wine's bouquet is its nose
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A floral arrangement greets a monarch from Viking times.
explanation.definitionFit: Norse describes medieval Scandinavia, its people and their language.

clue.text: Hero-worship from frivolous viewers reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the phrase is to be heard spoken

parts.note: idle eyes: idle means frivolous, eyes are what we view with

explanation.surface: Fan adulation coming from shallow television audiences, so they say.
explanation.definitionFit: To idolise someone is to adore them uncritically, worshipping them as a hero.

clue.text: No way booze is remedy against ills

parts.note: ST, street, is a way
rum is a kind of booze

explanation.surface: A cure-all claim: there is no road by which drink cures sickness.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostrum is a quack medicine or pet scheme claimed to cure every ailment.

clue.text: Philosopher remapped argosy path

indicators.note: remapped means laid out again differently, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A thinker redraws the route taken by a merchant fleet.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek thinker of Samos, famous for his theorem, was a philosopher and mathematician.

clue.text: Typically long vessel — see one in Bremen

parts.note: V stands for vide, Latin for see
ein is German for one, and Bremen is a German city

explanation.surface: A lengthy ship spotted in a German port.
explanation.definitionFit: Veins are the blood vessels carrying blood to the heart, usually long and narrow.
